headline: The Hire More Heroes Act of 2014 would have let employers leave out workers covered by Defense Department or VA health programs when counting toward the Affordable Care Act's large-employer rule.
what_it_does: It would have changed the tax code so that, when deciding whether an employer counts as an applicable large employer under the Affordable Care Act, the employer could exclude employees who have coverage through a Department of Defense health program, such as TRICARE, or through the Department of Veterans Affairs. Under the ACA, applicable large employers must offer health coverage to their employees, so this change would have affected whether some employers were required to do so. The bill's summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.group: Employers near the ACA large-employer threshold
who_it_affects.how: Employers that would otherwise be required to offer health coverage could have been able to exclude employees with TRICARE or VA coverage when counting their workforce.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and military families with TRICARE or VA health coverage
who_it_affects.how: Employees who have this coverage would have been excluded from the employer headcount used to decide whether their employer must offer ACA health coverage.

who_it_affects.group: Employees of employers that might no longer be required to offer coverage
who_it_affects.how: Workers at affected employers might not have been offered employer-sponsored health coverage if their employer fell below the large-employer threshold after the exclusion.
